problem: VLN with high-level goal-driven instructions (REVERIE, SOON) is trained on fewer than 60 MP3D buildings and about 10K trajectories, so models overfit seen environments and generalize poorly. Prior augmentation stays within the same few environments, and web image-caption data cannot be used to train a navigation policy.
motivation: Manually collecting VLN data is expensive and does not scale. HM3D offers 900 diverse, unlabeled buildings. Large pretrained 2D vision and language models could turn them into VLN training data, and environment diversity may matter more than the number of samples.
key_idea: Automatically build a large VLN dataset (HM3D-AutoVLN) from 900 unlabeled HM3D buildings, using auto-generated navigation graphs, 3D pseudo object labels merged from 2D Mask2Former predictions by cross-view consistency, and a GPT-2 speaker prompted with object labels to write instructions. Then pretrain and co-train VLN agents on it.
insight: Diversity of environments matters more than instruction count. With the same number of instructions (51,018 or 99,224), spanning 900 environments beats 200 or 400, and gains have not saturated at 900. Cross-view 3D fusion raises pseudo-label accuracy from 37.4% to 58.3% on 300 manually checked boxes, and the GPT-2 speaker beats template and LSTM speakers on captioning quality and downstream SR (55.89 vs 52.20 and 49.59). Joint fine-tuning on HM3D and REVERIE gives higher SR than fine-tuning on REVERIE alone (55.89 vs 50.87), which suggests that fine-tuning on the downstream data alone causes forgetting. Object grounding (RGS) improves only modestly because the instructions are not discriminative enough for specific object instances.
method: Navigation graph construction: sample 20,000 navigable points per building and greedily add nodes more than 2 m apart. Connect nodes if the geodesic distance is under 3 m and the mean depth between them exceeds 2 m. Render 36 RGB-D views per node.

3D pseudo object labeling: run Mask2Former (ADE20K) on all views and project the masks to 3D point clouds with depth. Voxelize at 0.1 m, average class probabilities per voxel, take the argmax, and group neighboring same-class voxels into 3D objects.

Triplet generation: for each 3D object, pick graph nodes where it is visible within d_o = 2 m as goals. Sample a start node 4-9 steps away and use the shortest path as the expert trajectory. The final panorama is used for instruction generation.

Speaker with object prompts: a transformer encodes the target-object token, other-object tokens and view-image tokens (label, location, size, visual feature, orientation) and averages each group into 3 prompt tokens. A GPT-2 decoder conditioned on these tokens is fine-tuned end-to-end on REVERIE instructions.
Stage I pretraining of DUET on HM3D-AutoVLN with MLM, single-step action prediction (SAP) and object grounding (OG). SAP samples STOP, next-step and random-node histories.

Stage II fine-tuning with the pseudo interactive demonstrator (student forcing). Either fine-tune on the downstream dataset only, or jointly train on a size-balanced mix of HM3D-AutoVLN and the downstream data to avoid forgetting.
Result: 36,562 nodes, 172,000 3D objects and 217,703 object-instruction-trajectory triplets over 900 buildings.

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer) with ViT-B/16 features and a GPT-2 speaker; also EnvDrop, RecBERT and HAMT trained with the data
setting.training_data: Pretraining on HM3D-AutoVLN (900 HM3D buildings, 217,703 auto-generated instructions) plus the downstream REVERIE or SOON training data. The speaker is fine-tuned on REVERIE. Mask2Former is pretrained on ADE20K and ViT-B/16 on ImageNet.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB-D (36 views per node) with GPS position
setting.action_space: Discrete navigation-graph viewpoints (topological map with global planning) plus a STOP action, and object selection or grounding
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D graph construction); MP3D simulator for REVERIE and SOON
setting.privileged: none at test time (the 2D detector's object boxes are used on SOON; REVERIE provides GT object boxes as part of the task). GT annotations are not used to build HM3D-AutoVLN.

numbers.extra: HM3D-AutoVLN pretraining (217,703 instructions) and joint fine-tuning

results: HM3D-AutoVLN pretraining lifts DUET on REVERIE val-unseen from SPL 33.73 to 40.85 (+7.1) and SR 46.98 to 55.89. On REVERIE test-unseen SPL rises from 36.06 to 38.88. On SOON val-unseen SPL rises from 22.58 to 30.69 (+8.1), and on test-unseen from 21.42 to 27.83. It also improves EnvDrop, RecBERT and HAMT, with the largest gains for high-capacity models. Grounding gains are smaller.
limitations: Generated instructions are not discriminative enough to pick a specific instance or spatial relation, so RGS and RGSPL gain little.
Pseudo 3D labels are noisy (58.3% correct on the manual sample), and far or small objects hurt performance.
Only discrete-graph, high-level-instruction VLN is studied, with the speaker fine-tuned on REVERIE only. Agents often fail to stop at the right location.
